title: tg-cli configuration
description: Canonical config.yaml settings for tg and tg-ctl. Credentials belong in .env. See tg help config for runtime compatibility and precedence.

enabled.description: Allow tg's lazy autostart of tg-ctl after a successful send from a detected agent inside tmux. This switch does not disable buttons or registrations, stop a running daemon, or block explicit daemon starts.

transport.description: Legacy transport selector. auto and tmux retain the current routing; channel is reserved and currently logs a warning and falls back to tmux.

session.description: Pin tmux discovery to this session name. An explicit session registration from tg-ctl start --session takes precedence; omit to auto-discover.

inject_wrap.description: Template around inbound text. Placeholders: {name} is the sender name, {msg} is the message text, and {id} is its tg# message reference.

staleness_sec.description: Legacy age setting in seconds, retained for compatibility. The daemon does not drop inbound messages by age.

idle_exit_min.description: Minutes without a live agent before the daemon exits. Agents outside tmux and recent registrations also count as activity.

allowed_senders.description: Additional allowed Telegram user IDs as a comma-separated scalar (for example "123, 456") or a single integer. An empty string adds none. YAML arrays are not supported.

topics.description: Enable forum-topic routing in a supergroup. Requires a forum supergroup with the bot allowed to manage topics.

private_topics.description: Enable topics for sessions in a private bot chat. If the bot lacks the private-topic capability, session creation asks whether to continue without topics or cancel. Topic-creation API errors fall back to flat-chat behavior with a diagnostic.

git_state_banner.description: Prepend a warning when a fresh non-reply message is automatically routed into a pane whose repository has uncommitted changes or a non-main branch.

server.description: Client machine only: the ssh_config alias of the host that runs tg-ctl, as ssh://<alias> (alias or host name only: no user, port, path or leading dash; key, port, jump host and host-key pinning belong in ~/.ssh/config). Setting it makes this machine a ctl client: tg-ctl run/start/restart/enable exit 78 and tg never autostarts a daemon. Requires control.machine; a machine is a client or the daemon host, never both.

machine.description: Client machine only: this machine's name in the server's routes and history, 1-32 characters of a-z, 0-9 and -, starting with a letter. Required with control.server.

remote_machines.description: Daemon host only: comma-separated name=ssh-target list of the client machines this tg-ctl serves (at most 8, unique names; target is [user@]host). It is both the allowlist of peers and the address replies are delivered to. Not allowed together with control.server or control.machine.

voice.description: Local transcription of inbound voice notes.

enabled.description: Enable local transcription of inbound voice notes. A usable binary and model are required; tg voice setup discovers or installs them and writes this block. An explicit false opts out of automatic setup.

runner.description: Local Whisper runner. whisper.cpp uses a native executable; faster-whisper uses a Python environment. Setup may choose a runner suited to the host.

bin_path.description: Path to whisper-cli (or its legacy main executable) for whisper.cpp, or to the virtual-environment Python executable for faster-whisper.

model_path.description: Path to a ggml model file for whisper.cpp, or a model-size token (such as large-v3-turbo) or converted model directory for faster-whisper.

language.description: Language token passed to the runner, or auto for automatic language detection. An empty value resolves to auto.

threads.description: CPU thread count. Omit to use the physical core count. A custom faster-whisper transcription script must accept --threads when this setting is supplied.

features.description: Outbound feature flags. --feature and --no-feature override these values.

autolink-tasks.description: Resolve Linear task references and add task links and titles to outbound messages.

autolink-prs.description: Resolve GitHub issue and pull-request references against the current repository and add links and titles.

autolink-msgrefs.description: Recognize tg# message references and link them when the chat supports a message URL.

autolink-msgref-preview.description: Quote a referenced Telegram message inline when local history contains it. Requires autolink-msgrefs.

md-as-pdf.description: Convert explicitly attached Markdown files to PDF for readable Telegram previews.

code-as-pdf.description: Convert explicitly attached code and configuration files to a mobile-sized, highlighted PDF. --with-original and --no-pdf adjust attachment behavior.

attach-denylist.description: Refuse explicit attachments that look like secret files, including environment files, keys, and credentials.

flood-cap.description: Limit the number of Telegram messages produced by one fragmented send.

cjk-guard.description: Reject isolated CJK characters inside otherwise Latin or Cyrillic words and mixed-script garbage tokens; ordinary CJK text remains supported.

screenshot-guard.description: Require a photo attachment when the caption or title claims to show a screenshot.

file-mention-guard.description: Refuse an agent message that names an existing local document without attaching it, and suggest the explicit --file command.

hooks.description: Run pre-send-photo hooks when hook descriptors are installed. AGENTS_HOOKS=0 bypasses these hooks.

laya.description: Laya, the local model tg asks about reports. tg starts it when it is not running. Read and validated by the Python caller (src/tgcli/laya): an invalid block exits 78 where Laya is consulted.

enabled.description: Ask Laya about reports at all. false (or TG_LAYA=0) switches the model off: the deterministic checks decide alone and no hint is printed on the ask path. Incompatible with required: true.

autostart.description: When no live Laya server answers, start one with `task classify-server start` (bounded by cold_timeout_sec). A failed start is not retried for 300 seconds. TG_LAYA_AUTOSTART overrides. --dry-run never starts anything.

required.description: Fail a send (exit 1, before any Telegram request) when Laya was consulted and is unavailable for any reason, instead of falling back to the deterministic checks with a hint. TG_LAYA_REQUIRED overrides. Cannot be combined with enabled: false or TG_LAYA=0 (exit 78).

cold_timeout_sec.description: Seconds allowed for the autostart (spawn plus model load). Measured cold start: 6.4 s on a CPU host; task classify-server start itself waits up to 60 s, so the default leaves room for its own diagnostic. TG_LAYA_COLD_TIMEOUT_SEC overrides.

warm_timeout_ms.description: Milliseconds allowed for one request to a running server. Measured warm calls: 31-64 ms (GPU/fast host), 267-1395 ms (CPU host, the first call being the slowest). TG_LAYA_TIMEOUT_MS overrides.

task_bin.description: Absolute path of the task executable used for autostart. Without it tg searches PATH entries that are absolute, not world-writable and owned by you or root, never the current directory. A path that is relative, missing or not executable is an error, not a fallback.

socket.description: Absolute path of a private Unix socket served by an external Laya (for example a proxy to another machine). Pins it durably: tg uses exactly this socket, never starts `task` or any model for it, and an unreachable pinned socket is an unavailable Laya (with laya.required: true the send fails). The parent directory must be owned by you with no group/other access and the socket must be yours. Relative, empty or `..`-containing values are an error (exit 78). TG_LAYA_SOCKET overrides.
